glosses: Able to read and write; having literacy.

examples.text: Intelligence tests are biased toward the literate.

Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Monday (September 8, 2025) declared Himachal as a “fully literate State” on the occasion of International Literary Day. […] Journey from 7% to 99.30%: The Chief Minister said Himachal Pradesh had reached this goal well before the scheduled timeframe, adding that the journey from minimal literacy rate of around 7% to full literacy had been full of challenges, yet the State had consistently moved forward with the aim of providing quality education. […] Mr. Sukhu said the literacy rate in Himachal Pradesh had reached 99.30%, which is higher than the national benchmark of 95% […] Union Education Secretary Sanjay Kumar, in a video message, congratulated Himachal Pradesh on this achievement and emphasised the importance of providing skill-based education to the newly literate.

glosses: Knowledgeable in literature, writing; literary; well-read.

examples.text: The reason literature plays a unique role in any literate culture is its longevity.

examples.text: The Mongol emperor Kublai Khan even commissioned an alphabetic script for his empire, to be used officially for all its literate languages, Mongolian, Chinese, Turkic and Persian.

glosses: A person who is able to read and write.

glosses: Exactly as stated; read or understood without interpretation; according to the letter; not figurative or metaphorical; following the letter or exact words; not taking liberties; etymonic rather than idiomatic.

examples.text: The literal translation of Spanish irse al otro barrio is "to go to the other neighbourhood" but it means "to die".
A literal reading of the law would prohibit it, but that is clearly not the intent.
a middle course between the rigour of literal translations and the liberty of paraphrasts

Within the constraints set by the original texts and by the mandates of the Division, the Committee has followed the maxim, 'As literal as possible, as free as necessary.' As a consequence, the New Revised Standard Version (NRSV) remains essentially a literal translation.

glosses: Actual, real, physical.

examples.text: Mechanically, operating this hybrid vehicle is sort of a cross between driving a car and taming an animal, which means the movie treats the audience to the sight of a man (pretending to be a teenager) driving a literal monster truck in a field next to a woman (also pretending to be a teenager) riding a horse.

glosses: That which generally assumes that the plainest reading of a given text is correct but which allows for metaphor where context indicates it.
Following the historical-grammatical method of biblical interpretation.

examples.text: It is most important to distinguish literalistic from literal interpretation. [...] ‘Literalistic’ interpretation is like word-for-word translation that yields the verbally exact or ‘formally equivalent’ versions but also runs the risk of overlooking the main (illocutionary) point. Literal interpretation, on the other hand, is more like a translation that strives for dynamic equivalence and yields the literary sense.

glosses: Consisting of, or expressed by, letters (of an alphabet); using literation.

examples.text: a literal equation

glosses: Unimaginative; matter-of-fact; literal-minded.
Used nonliterally as an intensifier. See literally for usage notes.

examples.text: Telemarketers are the literal worst.

glosses: Vu avec la lettre et la règle grammaticale, conforme à la lettre grammairienne.

examples.text: En vain donc ces dangereux interprètes nous crient que le gros des Pères n’a jamais examiné critiquement, le vrai ou le faux des explications littérales de la Bible ; qu’aussi la Tradition varie fort sur cela ; […].
Je m’inquiète pour mes enfants : ne vais-je pas en faire des sociopathes, au sens littéral, si je les gronde dès lors qu’ils s’approchent d’autres personnes ?

glosses: Qui prend un texte mot à mot.

examples.text: On a pris ce vers d’Homère non dans un sens littéral, mais dans un sens figuré.
Voici des exemples de traduction littérale, « mot à mot », tout à fait valables : I drink two cups of tea each morning. = Je bois deux tasses de thé chaque matin.
En quelque sorte un mot a toujours plusieurs significations comme c’est le cas dans la langue bamiléké. Il a donc une signification sémantique, figurative, littérale et symbolique.

glosses: Écrite, en parlant d’une langue.

examples.text: L’arabe littéral est l’arabe écrit, par opposition aux dialectes arabo-berbères parlés.

glosses: Exprimées par une lettre, en parlant d’une grandeur.

examples.text: Des grandeurs littérales.

glosses: Qui utilise des caractères alphabétiques.

examples.text: Le signal-texte dynamique KXC50 est mobile, porté par un véhicule ou une remorque. Il affiche, en caractères L11, un message littéral lumineux utilisé pour préciser ou compléter une information délivrée par un signal temporaire de type K ou AK ou encore pour délivrer une information lorsqu'on ne dispose pas du ou des signaux adéquats.

glosses: Valeur introduite explicitement dans le texte d’un programme.

examples.text: En C, le type des littéraux numériques peut être forcé par un suffixe.
